meta.title: Kubernetes vs Docker Swarm: Container Orchestration Comparison
meta.description: Structured comparison of Kubernetes and Docker Swarm for container orchestration across scalability, operational complexity, ecosystem, and production readiness.

kubernetes.notes: High complexity; kubeadm, kubectl, control plane setup; managed options (GKE/EKS) ease this significantly

docker_swarm.notes: docker swarm init; docker stack deploy; operational in minutes on existing Docker hosts

kubernetes.notes: Steep; Pods, Deployments, Services, Ingress, ConfigMaps, RBAC, Helm; significant investment

docker_swarm.notes: Docker Compose syntax familiar; services, stacks, secrets map naturally from existing Docker knowledge

kubernetes.notes: Proven at Google/Netflix/Spotify scale; horizontal pod autoscaling, cluster autoscaling, 5,000 node clusters

docker_swarm.notes: Handles hundreds of nodes; adequate for most SMBs; not battle-tested at hyperscale

kubernetes.notes: Multi-master etcd cluster; pod disruption budgets; rolling updates; self-healing

docker_swarm.notes: Raft consensus for manager HA; service restart on failure; less granular control

kubernetes.notes: Helm, Kustomize, ArgoCD, Istio, Prometheus, Grafana; dominant CNCF ecosystem

docker_swarm.notes: Minimal third-party tooling; Docker Compose and Docker CLI; no Helm equivalent

kubernetes.notes: CNI plugins (Calico, Flannel, Cilium); NetworkPolicies; Ingress controllers; service mesh support

docker_swarm.notes: Overlay networks built-in; simpler but less configurable; no NetworkPolicy equivalent

kubernetes.notes: PersistentVolumes, StorageClasses, CSI plugins; dynamic provisioning; stateful workloads

docker_swarm.notes: Volumes work but complex for distributed storage; fewer native options for stateful apps

kubernetes.notes: RBAC, PSA, OPA/Gatekeeper, Secrets encryption at rest, NetworkPolicy, mTLS via Istio

docker_swarm.notes: Secrets management, TLS auto-rotation for manager comms; limited RBAC; no policy engine

kubernetes.notes: Native to GitOps (ArgoCD, Flux); all major CI tools have K8s deployment plugins

docker_swarm.notes: Works with CI tools via docker stack deploy; less ecosystem support than K8s

kubernetes.notes: Prometheus + Grafana standard stack; distributed tracing via OpenTelemetry; structured logging

docker_swarm.notes: Basic docker service logs; no native metrics; requires external tools with less integration

kubernetes.notes: CNCF graduated project; thousands of contributors; 10-year industry standard trajectory

docker_swarm.notes: Docker Inc. reduced investment; community maintenance mode; Mirantis acquired Docker; uncertain future

kubernetes.notes: High: control plane cost on managed ($70 to $200+/mo on EKS/GKE) + engineering time

docker_swarm.notes: No control plane overhead; runs on existing VMs; minimal operational burden

use_case_recommendations.reason: Lower overhead, faster setup, sufficient for most SMB production workloads
Battle-tested HA, RBAC, autoscaling, and ecosystem make it the production standard
Mirrors production compose files; fast iteration; no cloud control plane cost
Namespace isolation, NetworkPolicies, and RBAC enable secure tenant separation
Minimal migration effort; Compose files translate directly to Swarm stacks
Richer security primitives; audit logging; policy enforcement via OPA; managed K8s compliance certs
